info.title: Sphericon Site API
info.description: The API of the Sphericon web app, authenticated by the session cookie.

post.description:
Confirm an email change from the token sent to the new address. Public:
the link may be opened from a browser without a session. The change ends
every session of the user (ADR 0020); when the request carries a valid
session of that same user, it continues under the fresh cookie set in this
response. The link alone never starts a session.

parameters.name: JWT
parameters.description: The confirming browser's session, if any

Set-Cookie.description: The confirming session reissued, set when the request carried one

post.description:
Request a password-reset link. Always returns 202 regardless of whether
the email matches an account and even when the address has used its hourly
mail budget, to avoid leaking which addresses exist. Answers 429 over the
per-IP limit.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The request budget of the window that was exceeded

post.description:
Check the password. A User without a Second factor gets a session (outcome
`session`, the JWT cookie set here); a User with one gets outcome `challenge`,
a short-lived single-use challenge for the second step and no cookie (ADR
0020). Unknown email and wrong password answer the same 401; failures feed the
Login throttle, which answers 429 even for a correct password while its delay
runs (ADR 0025). Only a started session resets the throttle's counter. An
Unverified User (ADR 0030) answers 403 with code `email_verification_required`
before any password check or second-factor challenge, and no session.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie, set when the outcome is `session`

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The request budget of the window that was exceeded

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time at which the window resets

post.description:
End the session on this browser: clears the session cookie. Answered while an
acceptance is pending (ADR 0062), so a gated User can sign out.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

Set-Cookie.description: The expired session cookie

post.description:
Begin a Passkey login: the request options for the browser, with the challenge in a signed,
httpOnly cookie. Anonymous and stateless: nothing is written until the login finishes, so
the call cannot be used to fill a table (ADR 0052). 404 when the Instance has no host name
a Passkey can be bound to.

Set-Cookie.description: The ceremony cookie carrying the challenge

post.description:
Finish a Passkey login: the authenticator's response, with no email and no password. The
User is found by the credential id; the authenticator must have verified the person and the
challenge must not have been used before. A Passkey replaces the password and the Second
factor, so the session cookie is set at once (ADR 0052). Every failure (an unknown credential,
a response that does not verify, a spent or expired challenge, an Unverified User) answers
the same 401 and counts against no one; while a known User's Login throttle delay runs the
answer is 429 (ADR 0025).

Set-Cookie.description:
The session cookie (always set here; optional only because the response shares its
shape with the login operation's)

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The request budget of the window that was exceeded

post.description:
Send the verification link again to an Unverified User. Answers 202 the same
way whether the address is unknown, already verified or unverified, so it adds no
enumeration; only an Unverified User gets a mail. Rate limited per IP
like Sign-up.

Set a new password from a reset token. A password outside the length rule answers 422

The second login step of a User with a Second factor: verify the challenge

forged challenge and a wrong code answer the same 401; wrong codes feed the
Login throttle of the User's address, which answers 429 even for a correct code
while its delay runs (ADR 0020, ADR 0025).

post.description:
Create an Unverified User (ADR 0030): no session, no Workspace. A verification
email with the link is on its way (202), and 202 is the answer for every address,
taken or not (ADR 0031): the owner of a taken address gets a notice by mail
instead. The answer always sets the Sign-up browser cookie (httpOnly, SameSite=Strict,
scoped to the auth prefix shared by verify and resend), which binds the link to this browser, so the
header does not say whether the address is taken either. The password is required
(422 otherwise). On an Instance that does not require email verification (the selfhosted Mode) there is no
mail to carry that notice and no link: the request creates a Verified User with its
first Workspace at once (202, no session and no cookie: the User signs in next), and
a taken address answers 409. Sign-up is open on every Instance (ADR 0063).

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

Set-Cookie.description: The Sign-up browser cookie, absent when the install does not require verification

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The request budget of the window that was exceeded

post.description:
Undo a silent link from the notice mailed to the owner (ADR 0048): the token names
one Linked identity of the User, which is unlinked, and every session of the User ends.
Public: the link may be opened from a browser without a session. A link works once; one
whose identity is gone answers 400.

Complete a pending sign-up with the answers to the Sign-up items: creates the User with its
Verified email, its Linked identity, its first Workspace (and the Membership of the
Invitation the flow began from) and the Consent records (source `provider_screen`) in one
transaction, and starts the session. A required acceptance not ticked answers 422 under
`signupItems.<key>` and keeps the pending sign-up; an item not in effect or a stale version
answers 422 under `signupItems`. An expired, completed, declined or forged token answers 400,
and so does one whose address or provider account was taken meanwhile.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie of the new User

post.description:
Decline a pending sign-up: it is deleted and nothing is created. Answers 204 also for a
token that names nothing any more.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

get.description:
The Sign-in providers this Instance offers, for the buttons of the login and sign-up
pages. Public; empty when none is configured.

Where the provider sends the browser back (the redirect URI derived from the app URL).
Always answers 302: to `return_to` (or `/`) with the session cookie when the sign-in
succeeds, and to `/login?error=<code>` (see SiteSigninError) when it does not. A known
identity signs in; a new, trusted email creates a Verified User with its first Workspace
and no mail; while the Instance has Sign-up items in effect it creates no User yet and the
redirect is to `/signin-pending?token=<reference>` (plus `redirect` when the flow had a
`return_to`), the screen that asks the items and completes the sign-up through
`/auth/signin-pending` (ADR 0062). A User with a Second factor gets no session and no cookie: the redirect is
to `/login?challenge=<token>`, the challenge of `/auth/second-factor` (ADR 0020), which
a TOTP or Recovery code finishes under the Login throttle. Every parameter is optional so that a denied consent (`error` only) or a
stray visit reaches the handler and gets the same redirect as any other refusal.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The flow's `state`, echoed by the provider

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: The provider's error code, present when consent was denied or the request failed

parameters.name: JWT
parameters.description:
The session cookie: read only when the flow is a link (it names a User), which
must be completed by the browser that is signed in as that User

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie on success; the expired flow cookie on a refusal

get.description:
Start a sign-in with a Sign-in provider: draws the flow's `state`, PKCE verifier and
`nonce`, keeps them (with the validated `return_to`) in a short-lived signed cookie
(httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, scoped to the signin prefix) and redirects (302) the browser to
the provider. `return_to` is honoured only as a relative in-app path; anything else
is dropped. 404 for a provider that is not configured.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: A relative in-app path to land on after signing in

parameters.name: invitation
parameters.description:
The token of an Invitation link: the sign-in then accepts that Invitation when the
provider's trusted email is the invited address, and an Invitation opens a closed
Sign-up for that address (ADR 0042). A mismatch creates nothing.

Set-Cookie.description: The flow cookie

post.description:
Complete a Sign-up from the verification link (the token is the
credential): stamps the Verified email, ends every earlier session, creates the
User's first Workspace, sends the welcome email and starts the session (the cookie
is issued after the epoch bump, as login does, ADR 0020). When the request carries
the Sign-up browser cookie the link was minted for, the password from Sign-up
stays; otherwise the request must carry a password, which replaces it, and without
one the answer is 428 and nothing changes, the link stays valid (a mail scanner
consumes nothing); a password outside the length rule answers 422, and the link stays
valid too. A link is single use and scoped to the address it was sent to.
Rate limited like Sign-up.

parameters.name: SIGN_UP_BROWSER
parameters.description:
The Sign-up browser cookie of the browser that signed up, if any. Its path is the
auth prefix shared with resend, and it is SameSite=Strict: not sent on the
cross-site click from the mail, but sent on the page's own later request.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie of the verified User

428.description:
RFC 7807 precondition required response: the request needs something it did not carry
(a verification link opened outside its Sign-up browser needs a password, ADR 0030)

post.description:
Perform a double opt-in confirmation (ADR 0013). The deliberate human act
behind the confirmation page's button. Repeating it is a no-op. 410 means the
link has expired, so the page offers to sign up again; 400 is an invalid token.

post.description:
Accept an invite: create or complete the User, or attach the signed-in Verified
User, and create the Membership. 401 without a session and 403 for another User's
session when the address has a Verified User.

get.description:
The current version of a Sign-up item's Legal document, for its public page. Public. 404
for an unknown or archived item and for one with no published version. Answered while an
acceptance is pending, for the screen that shows the new texts (ADR 0062).
Get the authenticated user's profile

put.description:
Update the authenticated user's profile (name, time zone and/or password). A password
change ends every session of the user (ADR 0020); the acting one continues
under the fresh session cookie set in this response. A wrong current password feeds the
Login throttle, which answers 429 even for a right one while its delay runs.

Set-Cookie.description: The acting session reissued, set when the password changed

429.description: RFC 7807 too many requests response: a rate limit was exceeded (ADR 0025)

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The request budget of the window that was exceeded

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time at which the window resets

post.description:
Accept every required acceptance pending for the User (ADR 0062): each is recorded accepted
with the source re-acceptance, and the next request is no longer refused. The body names each
pending item at the version the screen showed; 422 when one is missing or its version is no
longer the current one (a newer version was published meanwhile), and nothing is recorded.
With nothing pending it records nothing.

Delete the User, immediately and irreversibly (User deletion, ADR 0050): every Membership,
Linked identity, the Second factor and the Recovery codes go, every session ends (the
cookie is cleared here) and one email tells the address. Needs the User's own email, the
password (a User with no password, signed in only through a Sign-in provider, sends the
token of the link mailed by `deleteUserLink` instead: 400 when it is expired, used, or
was issued to another User) and, with a Second factor, a current code. 403 on a wrong
password or code (both feed the Login throttle: 429 while its delay runs). 422 when the typed email is not the
User's, or while the User is the only Owner of a Workspace that is not in its deletion
window: the Workspaces are listed and nothing is deleted. A Workspace in its deletion
window does not block.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

Set-Cookie.description: The expired session cookie

422.description: RFC 7807 validation response of User deletion

429.description: RFC 7807 too many requests response: a rate limit was exceeded (ADR 0025)

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The request budget of the window that was exceeded

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window

post.description:
Mail the one-time deletion link to a User with no password (ADR 0050): it goes to the
User's Verified email, is bound to the User (not the address), expires after an hour and
works once. 202 whether or not a mail is due (a mail flood is throttled silently). 422
when the typed email is not the User's, or when the User has a password and confirms with
it instead.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

422.description: RFC 7807 validation response of User deletion

post.description:
Request an email change; sends a confirmation link to the new address.
Requires the current password. A taken address answers 202 like a free one: its
owner gets a notice by mail instead of the link (ADR 0031).

get.description: List the authenticated User's Linked identities

delete.description:
Unlink an identity. 409 when it would leave the User no way to sign in (no password
and no other identity). Every other session ends; the acting one continues under the
cookie set here.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

Set-Cookie.description: The acting session reissued under the new session epoch

get.description:
Start linking another Sign-in provider account to the authenticated User. Works like
`start` of a sign-in, but the flow cookie also names the User, and the shared callback
adds the provider's subject to that User whatever email the provider reports. The
callback redirects to `return_to` (default the account security page); a refusal goes
to the account security page with the `error` code (see SiteSigninError). 404 for a
provider that is not configured.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: A relative in-app path to land on afterwards

Set-Cookie.description: The flow cookie

get.description:
The optional consents in effect (not archived, with a published version) and the User's
current answer to each. They belong to the User, so no Workspace is read. Empty when the
Instance has none. A required acceptance and a notice are not listed: they are not the User's
to change.

put.description:
Give or withdraw an optional consent. Giving it records `accepted` on the current version,
withdrawing a given one records `withdrawn`, both with the source account settings; a change
that leaves the answer as it is records nothing. 404 for an item not in effect. 422 for a
required acceptance or a notice, which cannot be changed here, and for a version that is not
the current one (field `version`).

get.description: List the authenticated User's Passkeys

post.description:
Begin a fresh Passkey check: the request options for the browser, naming the User's own
Passkeys, with the challenge in a signed, httpOnly cookie. Nothing is written. The check
stands in for the password of a User who has none (ADR 0052). 404 when Passkeys are
unavailable or the User holds none.

Set-Cookie.description: The ceremony cookie carrying the challenge

post.description:
Finish a Passkey check. The authenticator must have verified the person, by a Passkey of
the session's own User, against a challenge not used before. The acting session is
reissued carrying the time of the check, which counts as the proof of identity for the
next few minutes; no session ends. 403 for any response that does not verify.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

Set-Cookie.description: The acting session reissued with the check

post.description:
Begin registering a Passkey: the creation options for the browser, with the challenge
in a signed, httpOnly cookie. Nothing is written: the ceremony is stateless until it
finishes (ADR 0051). The options exclude the Passkeys the User already holds.

Set-Cookie.description: The ceremony cookie carrying the challenge

post.description:
Finish registering a Passkey, proving the password (or a fresh provider login or Passkey check). The
authenticator must have verified the user and the challenge must not have been used
before. On success every other session ends, the acting one continues under the cookie
set here and the owner is mailed. 403 on a wrong password (it feeds the Login throttle:
429 while its delay runs), 422 when the ceremony fails: no ceremony cookie, an expired
or spent challenge, a response the library refuses, an authenticator that did not verify
the user, or a credential already registered.

Set-Cookie.description: The acting session reissued under the new session epoch

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window

patch.description:
Rename a Passkey of the authenticated User. 404 for an unknown Passkey or another User's,
422 for a name that is empty or longer than 100 characters.

delete.description:
Remove a Passkey of the authenticated User, proving the password (or a fresh provider
login). It no longer signs anyone in, every other session ends, the acting one continues
under the cookie set here and the owner is mailed. 403 on a wrong password (it feeds the
Login throttle: 429 while its delay runs), 404 for an unknown Passkey or another User's,
409 when it is the last way the User can sign in: no password, no Linked identity and no
other Passkey.

Set-Cookie.description: The acting session reissued under the new session epoch

get.description:
The authenticated User's Second factor status. Answered while an acceptance is pending, for
the account deletion form (ADR 0062).

post.description:
Disable the Second factor, proving the password and a current code. Every
other session ends; the acting one continues under the cookie set here. 403 on
a wrong password (it feeds the Login throttle: 429 while its delay runs), 422
on a wrong code, 409 without an active Second factor.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

Set-Cookie.description: The acting session reissued under the new session epoch

post.description:
Start enrolling a TOTP Second factor, proving the password: creates a pending
secret (replacing an earlier pending one). It counts as a Second factor only
once confirmed. 403 on a wrong password (or, for a User with no password, no provider sign-in or Passkey check in the last few minutes), 409 when a Second factor is already
active. A wrong password feeds the Login throttle, which answers 429 even for a
correct one while its delay runs (ADR 0025).

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time at which the window resets

post.description:
Confirm the pending enrollment with the password and a code from the app. On
success the Second factor is active, every other session ends and the acting
one continues under the cookie set here; the Recovery codes are returned once.
403 on a wrong password (or, for a User with no password, no provider sign-in or Passkey check in the last few minutes) (it feeds the Login throttle: 429 while its delay
runs), 422 on a wrong code, 409 without a pending enrollment.

Set-Cookie.description: The acting session reissued under the new session epoch

Replace the Recovery codes with a fresh set (the previous set stops working).
Every other session ends; the acting one continues under the cookie set here.
403 on a wrong password (or, for a User with no password, no provider sign-in or Passkey check in the last few minutes) (it feeds the Login throttle: 429 while its delay
runs), 409 without an active Second factor.

Set-Cookie.description: The acting session reissued under the new session epoch

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window

post.description:
Sign out everywhere: end every session of the user, on every device,
including the one making the request (its cookie is cleared).

post.description:
Answer the Sign-up survey. It belongs to the User, so it takes no Workspace. The answers
are stored and the User stops owing the survey in one transaction (204). 409 when the User
does not owe the survey: it was answered already, or the User was never asked (the
Instance has it off, or the User joined by an Invitation). 422 for a missing required
answer, a value outside the lists, an `…Other` text over its length or without its
`other` choice. Nothing is stored for a refused request.

Create a Workspace; the authenticated User becomes its Owner. Names are free text
and need not be unique. An Unverified User is refused with 403 and code
`email_verification_required`. The creation is recorded as an Audit entry.

get.description:
List the Workspaces in their deletion window that the authenticated User owns, with
the date their data will be erased. Answered while an acceptance is pending, for the
account deletion form (ADR 0062).

post.description:

pending-deletion freeze: a Workspace suspension or Staff hold stays. A deleted
Workspace is not exposed to anyone but its Owners, so a caller who is not an Owner
gets 404 as for an unknown one. A Workspace past its window, or already being
erased, answers 409; an erased one has no Owner left to ask, so it answers 404.
Recorded as an Audit entry.

never changes.

buttonTextColor.description: Color of the text on a button, `#rrggbb`

buttonRadius.description: Corner radius of a button in pixels, 0 to 32

footerText.description: Plain text printed under the starter messages, at most 500 characters; empty for none

SiteSaveBrandKitInput.description:
Save the Brand kit: the first save creates it and the starter Templates, a later one replaces
its values.

currentPassword.description:
Current password. Left out by a User with no password, who proves a provider or Passkey
sign-in of the last few minutes instead (ADR 0048).

SiteSecondFactorConfirmInput.description: Proof of the User's password (or a fresh provider login or Passkey check) and a code from the authenticator app

currentPassword.description:
Current password. Left out by a User with no password, who proves a provider or Passkey
sign-in of the last few minutes instead (ADR 0048).

SiteSecondFactorDisableInput.description: Proof of password (or a fresh provider login or Passkey check) and possession, for disabling the Second factor

otpauthUri.description: The otpauth:// URI the QR code encodes

qrCode.description: The QR code of the otpauth URI, as a PNG data URI

SiteSecondFactorEnrollment.description: A pending enrollment: the TOTP secret to add to an authenticator app

currentPassword.description:
Current password. Left out by a User with no password, who proves a provider or Passkey
sign-in of the last few minutes instead (ADR 0048).

SiteSecondFactorStartInput.description: Proof of the User's password (or a fresh provider login or Passkey check), for starting an enrollment

pending.description: Whether an enrollment was started and still awaits its confirmation code

recoveryCodesRemaining.description: Unused Recovery codes left (0 without a Second factor)

passwordSet.description:
Whether the User has a password. Without one, the steps that ask for the password
accept a fresh sign-in with a Sign-in provider instead.

identityProofFresh.description:
Whether the session holds a fresh proof that stands in for the password: a Sign-in
provider login or a Passkey check of the last few minutes (a User with a password always
proves the password). When a User with no password sees false, the next step is to sign
in with a provider again or to check a Passkey.

SiteSecondFactorStatus.description:
The authenticated User's Second factor (ADR 0020). Recovery codes are never
readable here: only how many are left.

condition.description: Segment condition: the tree of tests; an empty group matches all contacts

archivedAt.description: When the segment was archived; null while it is kept

SiteSegmentResource.description: Segment resource used by the site UI

dkimSelector.description: DKIM selector; the record host is "<selector>._domainkey.<domain>"

verified.description: Whether the domain is verified now: it has a `verifiedAt` and no `verificationLostAt` since

dkimRecord.description: The required DKIM TXT record (gates sending in a later slice)

spfRecord.description: The suggested SPF TXT record (advisory — does not gate)

dmarcRecord.description: The suggested DMARC TXT record (advisory bulk-readiness signal)

trackingRecord.description: The Tracking domain CNAME; absent when the instance has no tracking target configured

lastCheckedAt.description: When the DKIM DNS was most recently checked (null = never)

verifiedAt.description: When the domain most recently became verified (null = never); kept after a loss

verificationLostAt.description: When a re-check most recently found the verified DKIM DNS gone (null = not lost: never verified, or verified again since)

archivedAt.description: When the domain was archived; null while it is kept. An archived domain serves no Tracking domain host.

SiteSendingDomainResource.description:
Sending domain resource used by the site UI (ADR 0010). sphericon generates the
DKIM keypair; the user publishes the DKIM TXT to authenticate the domain. The
private key is never exposed. `verified` is re-checked in the background:
the domain loses it (`verificationLostAt`) if the DNS record disappears.

endpoint.description: Custom SES-compatible API endpoint (e.g. Yandex Cloud Postbox); empty for AWS

accessKeyIdLast4.description: Last 4 chars of the access key id, for recognition

SiteSesConfig.description: SES config without the secret access key

enabled.description: Whether to admit Users by Join domain from now on

SiteSetDomainJoinInput.description: Switch domain join on or off

SiteSetupProgress.description: The Workspace's Setup checklist: a point-in-time read model, never ticked by hand

SiteSetupStepStatus.description: Where one Setup checklist step stands, read off the Workspace's own data

integration.description: At least one real Integration exists; a Test inbox delivers nothing outside, so it does not count

sendingDomain.description: At least one Sending domain is verified; pending while one exists unverified

contact.description: At least one Contact exists, from any source

sentEmail.description: At least one Outbound message was sent, from any surface (a Test send is not one)

SiteSetupSteps.description: The Setup checklist steps, in the order the checklist shows them; none blocks another

password.description:
Required whenever sign-up is open. Stored hashed on the Unverified User; a repeated
Sign-up of the address replaces it.

signupItems.description:
The answers to the Sign-up items in effect (ADR 0062). Every required acceptance must be
answered ticked at its current version, or the field `signupItems.<key>` is refused; an
optional consent left out is not recorded. Each answered item is recorded as accepted or
declined, and each notice in effect as shown. Absent with no items in effect.

SiteSignUpInput.description:
Sign up with a name, an email and a password. The User stays Unverified until the
address is proven (ADR 0030); the password is trusted only when the verification link
is opened in the Sign-up browser.

SiteSigninError.description:
Why a provider sign-in did not start a session. The callback redirects to `/login` with
one of these as the `error` query parameter, and the SPA renders it through i18n.

SiteSigninNotMeInput.description: The "this was not me" link of the notice mailed when a Sign-in provider was linked to an account

token.description: The signed reference from the screen's URL
The signed reference from the screen's URL

signupItems.description:
The answers to the Sign-up items in effect, by the rules of the sign-up form's
`signupItems`

SiteSigninPendingSubmitInput.description: The answers that complete a pending sign-up

name.description: The registry name, the path segment of its `start` and `callback` operations

displayName.description: What the button says: the provider's own name (`Google`)

SiteSigninProvider.description: One Sign-in provider an Instance offers (ADR 0048)

SiteSigninProviders.description:
The Sign-in providers this Instance has configured. Empty on an Instance that
configured none, which leaves the login and sign-up pages as they are.

SiteSignupCompanySize.description: How many people work at the User's company (second question)

SiteSignupGoal.description: What the User mainly wants to do with the product (third question)

version.description: The label of the current version, the one a person accepts

SiteSignupItem.description:
A Sign-up item in effect, with the label of its current Legal document version: what the
sign-up form asks (ADR 0062)

version.description: The label of the version the form showed

accepted.description:
Whether the box was ticked; absent is unticked. A notice has no box, and its answer only
names the version shown.

SiteSignupItemAnswer.description:
A person's answer to one Sign-up item the form showed (ADR 0062). An item named that is not in
effect, a version that is not its current one, or an item named twice refuses the form.

SiteSignupItemList.description: The Sign-up items in effect, in the order of the sign-up form

SiteSignupRole.description: What the User does (Sign-up survey, first question)

SiteSignupSource.description: Where the User heard about the product (fourth question, optional)

roleOther.description: What the User does, when `role` is `other`

companySize.description: How many people work at the User's company

mainGoal.description: What the User mainly wants to do with the product

heardFrom.description: Where the User heard about the product

heardFromOther.description: Where the User heard about the product, when `heardFrom` is `other`

SiteSignupSurveyInput.description:
The answers to the Sign-up survey, sent once after its last screen. `role`, `companySize`
and `mainGoal` are required; `heardFrom` is optional. Each `…Other` text is allowed only
with its question's `other` choice.

SiteSoleOwnedWorkspace.description: A Workspace the User is the only Owner of, which blocks User deletion

SiteSuppressionChannel.description: The channel a suppression applies to (email today; sms reserved)

SiteSuppressionReason.description:
Why a destination is on the suppression (do-not-send) list. Unsubscribe is
not a suppression — it is a separate, per-source opt-out.

channel.description: The channel this suppression applies to

liftedAt.description: When the suppression was lifted; null while it is active. A lifted one no longer blocks sends.

SiteSuppressionResource.description: A suppressed destination: the send path skips it on every surface

SiteTagResource.description: A Tag: a presence-only, workspace-scoped label on Contacts (auto-created on first use).

from.description:
The From address of the preview. A Workspace with a verified Sending domain gets its own
domain; one without gets the System sender, which is not the address Contacts will see.

captured.description:
true when the Workspace's default Integration keeps what it is sent (a Test inbox): the
preview was captured there, not sent to the address named.

SiteTestSendBroadcastResult.description: What a test send did: the address the preview went out from

SiteTrackingReason.description: Why a Tracking domain is held back although its CNAME may be right: `host_taken` means another Workspace already has this host verified (ADR 0038)

host.description: The host to create the record at: "track." followed by the domain

target.description: The edge host the CNAME must point at

reason.description: Why the domain is not advancing; absent when nothing holds it back

lastCheckedAt.description: When the Tracking domain was most recently checked (null = never)

stateChangedAt.description: When the state most recently changed (null = never)

SiteTrackingRecord.description: The Tracking domain CNAME of a Sending domain (ADR 0038): `host` must point at `target`. Read-only; absent when the instance has no tracking target configured.

SiteTrackingState.description: State of a Tracking domain (ADR 0038): `pending` until the CNAME is found at the edge host, `dns_verified` once it is (the edge may provision), `serving` once HTTPS on the host answers; mail uses the host only while `serving`

SiteTransactionalEmailChannel.description: The channel a transactional send went out on (email today; sms reserved)

channel.description: The channel this send went out on

templateId.description: The id of the Template rendered at send time (bound by reference)

contactId.description: The contact this destination resolved to, when one existed

error.description: Provider error message, present when status is `failed`

captured.description: True when the send went through a Test inbox: captured, not delivered

SiteTransactionalEmailResource.description: One transactional send: the durable, read-only trace of an `/api/emails` call

exitEvents.description: Event actions that end an active enrollment early; replaces the list, omitted keeps it

goalEvent.description: Event action that ends an active enrollment as goal_reached; null removes it, omitted keeps it

integrationId.description: Sending integration of the email steps; null means the workspace default, omitted keeps it

SiteUpdateAutomationInput.description:
Site request body for updating an automation. The name changes at once; the trigger, steps
and integration write the draft (ADR 0065): omitted fields keep the draft's, else the live
version's, and publishing makes the draft live.

subjectId.description: The customer's own user id — an alias key

customFields.description: Typed custom field values keyed by the field's machine key

tags.description: The contact's complete tag set when given: tags not listed are removed from it, an absent key keeps them

SiteUpdateContactInput.description:
Site request body for updating a contact: the attributes /api takes, and its tag set. The
app's contact form sets the tags in the same save; /api tags a contact through its own
operations (`tags_apply`, `tags_remove`), which is why its body has no tags.

timezone.description:
New User time zone, an IANA name (422 when the zone database does not know it); null
clears it, so the app follows the browser again

currentPassword.description: Current password — required when changing the password

SiteUpdateMeInput.description:
Update the authenticated user's profile. To change the password, provide
both currentPassword and newPassword.

SiteUpdateMembershipInput.description: Change a member's role. Only an owner may grant/transfer the owner role.

reportingCurrency.description: The Reporting currency, an ISO 4217 code

attributionWindowDays.description: The Attribution window in whole days

SiteUpdateRevenueSettingsInput.description: Change the revenue settings; a field left out stays as it is

triggerEvents.description: The Event actions that make the Rule fire; at least one

actions.description: The Actions to run, in order

SiteUpdateRuleInput.description: Site request body for updating a Rule. The name is the Rule's own; the Trigger events, condition and Actions write the draft, and the ones left out keep the draft's, else the live version's.

condition.description: Segment condition: the tree of tests; an empty group matches all contacts

SiteUpdateSegmentInput.description: Site request body for updating a segment

postalAddress.description:
Physical postal address for the marketing email footer (CAN-SPAM). Omit to
leave it unchanged; send an empty string to clear it.

SiteUpdateWorkspaceInput.description: Update a workspace. The id is immutable (it is the route key); the display name and the CAN-SPAM postal address can change.

email.description: Email address (login identity; change it via the email-change flow)

emailVerified.description: Whether the user has confirmed ownership of their email

timezone.description:
The User time zone (ADR 0068): the IANA zone the app shows times in and the User's mail
prints dates in. Null follows the browser in the app and is UTC in mail. Reports count in
the Workspace time zone, never this one.

signupSurveyDue.description:
Whether the User owes the Sign-up survey: computed on the server, so the app reads this
one field and never the Instance setting. True after a public sign-up on an Instance that
asks, until the survey is answered.

acceptancesPending.description:
The required acceptances whose current version the User has not accepted, in the order of
the sign-up form (ADR 0062). While any is listed, every operation that is not marked
`x-allowed-while-acceptance-pending` refuses the User with 403 `acceptance_pending`; the app
shows the texts and accepts them with `acceptPending` before any other page. Empty for a User
who holds every current version.

password.description:
Needed only when the link is not opened in the Sign-up browser: it replaces
the password given at Sign-up. Ignored in the Sign-up browser.

SiteVerifyEmailInput.description: Prove an email address with the token sent to it

landingWorkspaceId.description:
The Workspace to open: the one the User joined by its Join domain (ADR 0051), else
the first Workspace made for them

SiteVerifyEmailResult.description: Where a User who proved their address goes next

SiteWebhookDisabledReason.description:
Why an endpoint is off. A closed set: `owner` (a member turned it off), `gone` (the
receiver answered 410 Gone) and `persistent_failure` (deliveries failed for longer
than the window). Absent while the endpoint is enabled.

url.description: Destination URL events are POSTed to

secret.description: HMAC signing secret (receivers verify the webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature headers, the Standard Webhooks scheme)

eventTypes.description: Event names this endpoint receives; empty means all events

enabled.description: Whether the endpoint receives deliveries: true while it has no `disabledAt`

disabledAt.description: When the endpoint was turned off; absent while it is enabled

disabledReason.description: Why the endpoint is off; present exactly when `disabledAt` is

failure.description: Present while deliveries are failing; cleared by the next 2xx

SiteWebhookEndpointResource.description: Webhook endpoint resource used by the site UI

SiteWebhookErrorKind.description:
Why a delivery to a webhook endpoint failed. A closed set: `timeout` (no answer in
time), `blocked_address` (the URL names an address this instance does not permit),
`http_status` (a non-2xx answer, see `status`) and `network` (any other transport
failure).

consecutiveFailures.description: Deliveries that failed in a row

since.description: When the current run of failures began

status.description: HTTP status of the latest failure; present only for kind `http_status`

SiteWebhookFailure.description: The failure state of an endpoint that is currently failing; absent while it is healthy.

status.description: HTTP status the receiver answered, when it answered

kind.description: Why the delivery failed; absent when delivered

SiteWebhookTestResult.description: What the receiver answered to a test delivery. The endpoint's failure state is not touched.

key.description: The setter's key, unique per Workspace

reasonCode.description: Machine reason code the setter gave

message.description: The setter's message for the Owner, to show as given

actionUrl.description: Where an Owner or Admin can resolve the hold, as the setter gave it; absent when none was given

SiteWorkspaceHold.description:
A Staff hold on the Workspace's outbound sending (ADR 0009), as the Workspace's
members see it. It is not a suspension: it is set from outside, carries its own
message, and lifts by itself at its expiry.

id.description:
The Workspace id: its short opaque public address and the route key for nested
workspace resources (ADR 0043)

collectKey.description: Per-workspace collect write-key (x-collect-key) for the tracking snippet

postalAddress.description:
Physical postal address printed in the marketing email footer (CAN-SPAM
15 U.S.C. §7704(a)(5)). Empty until the workspace sets one.

timezone.description:
The Workspace time zone (ADR 0057): the IANA name every analytics report counts its days
in. UTC until an Owner or Admin sets it.

role.description:
The authenticated User's role in this Workspace (from their Membership). It
rides the Workspace list so role-gated UI is known even while the Workspace's
own endpoints are withheld under a Two-factor requirement.

permissions.description:
The Permissions the authenticated User's Role holds in this Workspace (ADR 0061):
the client asks these whether to offer an action, it never computes them from the
Role.

suspendedAt.description:
When outbound sending was suspended (ADR 0007); absent while the workspace can
send. A suspension freezes every send surface but not login, reads or tracking.

suspensionReason.description: Why sending was suspended, shown to the owner; present only while suspended.

supportEmail.description:
Where to appeal a suspension by email (SPHERICON_SUPPORT_EMAIL); absent when the instance
configured none.

mcpUrl.description:
The public origin an AI agent connects to as `<mcpUrl>/mcp`: SPHERICON_MCP_URL when MCP has its
own host, otherwise the app origin.

trackerUrl.description:
The public origin the tracker snippet loads `/t.js` from and posts `/collect` to:
SPHERICON_TRACKER_URL when the tracker has its own host, otherwise the app origin.

holds.description:
The Staff holds active now, oldest key first; empty while nothing holds sending.
Any one freezes every send surface, like a suspension, but a lapsed hold is never
listed.

secondFactorRequiredAt.description:
When an Owner or Admin switched on the Two-factor requirement (ADR 0020);
absent while every member may work without a Second factor.

secondFactorGraceEndsAt.description:
When the authenticated User's grace under the Two-factor requirement ends:
7 days after the later of the requirement's start and their Membership's
creation. Absent without a requirement or once the User has a Second factor.
After it, every request to this Workspace answers 403 with code
second_factor_required until the User enrolls one.

accountLinkAvailable.description:
Whether the authenticated User may open the Account link: true only for an
Owner, and only on an installation configured for it.

SiteWorkspaceResource.description: Workspace the current user belongs to

timezone.description: An IANA time zone name such as `Europe/Berlin`; the zone database decides what is valid

email.description: Address to send the rendered preview to

TestSendBroadcastInput.description: Request body for a test send

eventType.description: The event name the sample carries, for example `contact.created`

TestWebhookInput.description: Request body for sending a sample event to a webhook endpoint

TokenOnlyScope.description: Scopes only an API token can hold, never an OAuth grant

fromName.description: Sender display name; null goes back to the integration's default

fromEmail.description: Sender email address: a changed value must be on a verified Sending domain of the workspace, or the write is a 422. An unchanged one is not re-checked, so a draft whose domain lost verification stays editable. Null goes back to the integration's default.

body.description: HTML body. Writing only a body clears the stored document. Write this or `doc`, not both.

doc.description:
The editor's JSON document, an opaque object checked by the server against the schema `email_schema` returns. The server renders the
body from it in the same save; a document that cannot be rendered is a 422 with the reason and nothing is stored.

segmentId.description: Target segment; null means all contacts. An archived segment is refused with 422.

integrationId.description: Sending integration; null means the workspace default. An archived integration is refused with 422.

UpdateBroadcastInput.description: Request body for updating a draft broadcast: an omitted field keeps its value, null clears it

subjectId.description: The customer's own user id — an alias key

customFields.description: Typed custom field values keyed by the field's machine key

UpdateContactInput.description: Request body for updating a contact

maxPerSecond.description: Provider limit: most messages per second (1 to 10 000); null clears the limit, omit to keep. An SES Integration with an `endpoint` cannot be left without it

maxPerDay.description: Provider limit: most messages per rolling 24 hours (1 to 100 000 000); null clears the limit, omit to keep. An SES Integration with an `endpoint` cannot be left without it

preset.description: Name of a Preset from `presets_list`; null removes it. Changing it requires `params` in full: no secret carries over

params.description: The Preset's params. A secret that is blank, omitted or `********` stays as saved; a new value rotates it (the old one stays valid until retired)

retireSecrets.description: Stop accepting the retiring value of every rotating secret

UpdateIntegrationInput.description: Update an Integration. Omit `config` to keep stored credentials; blank secret fields inside it keep the stored secret.

doc.description:
The editor's JSON document, an opaque object checked by the server against the schema `email_schema` returns. The server renders the
body from it in the same save; a document that cannot be rendered is a 422 with the reason and nothing is stored.

UpdateTemplateInput.description: Request body for updating a template

eventTypes.description: Event names to receive; empty means all events

UpdateWebhookInput.description: Request body for updating a webhook endpoint

kind.description: What kind of row it is

count.description:
How many rows the entry stands for; absent means one. An `enrollment` entry names the
Automation (id, name) and counts its Enrollments; a `message` entry names it and counts its
sent Outbound messages.

UsedBy.description:
A row that uses the one a removal was refused for: what a client shows to say what to
change first

UsedByKind.description:
What kind of row a refused removal names as a user of the row (ADR 0049). One value per kind
of live user a removal can find, so a client branches on it without parsing text.

WorkspaceId.description:
A Workspace id (ADR 0043): 8 random base62 characters, assigned once at creation and the
Workspace's one public address.
